The results show that the proposed controller rapidly mitigates CM disturbances while maintaininghigh-qualityACcurrentwaveformsinthefour-legconfiguration. Finally, the hardware performance of an SST prototype is evaluated. In particular, the ability of the SST to safely redirect and absorb CM currents is demonstrated, showing how it can protect neighboring conventional transformers in the system. INTRODUCTION Today,avarietyofman-madeandnaturaleventsthreatenthereliableoperationoftheelectricpower grid, including high-altitude electromagnetic pulses (HEMP) and solar geomagnetic disturbances (GMD) [1, 2, 3]. During such events, changes in the Earth’s magnetic field — caused by a nuclear explosion or charged particles from a coronal mass ejection — create time- and spatially- varyingelectromagneticfieldsattheEarth’ssurface. Couplingwithlongtransmissionlines,these fields can induce low-frequency common-mode (CM) currents in grounded power transformers. These geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) can drive half-cycle saturation of transformer cores, resulting in distorted AC waveforms, increased losses, thermal stress, and, in severe cases, extendedpowersystemdisruption[2,3].
